title.en: Fencing a garden vs laying grass tiles

text.en:
Grandma needed wire fencing around her flowerbed AND square grass mats to cover its soil.
"Wait—are fencing and grass measured differently?" wondered Rohan.

Perimeter is the total distance along the outer boundary of a closed shape—like walking round a park or putting wire fencing round a field, measured in cm or m.
For a rectangle, Perimeter = 2 × (length + breadth); for a square or any regular polygon, Perimeter = number of sides × side length.
Area is the surface space enclosed inside a closed figure, counted in unit squares (sq cm or sq m): Rectangle Area = length × breadth, Square Area = side × side.
Two measurements rule farming, tailoring and architecture: Perimeter measures the border, while Area measures the flat inside.

board.text: Perimeter = outside walk; Area = inside cover

text.en: Imagine pacing along every outer edge of a closed figure—add all side lengths to get the Perimeter (in cm, m or km).
On a rectangle with length l and breadth b, opposite sides match, so Perimeter = 2 × (l + b).
For an equilateral triangle, Perimeter = 3 × side; for a square, 4 × side; for a regular pentagon, 5 × side!
Now look inside the boundary: Area counts how many 1 cm × 1 cm (or 1 m × 1 m) square tiles cover the surface completely.

board.text: Area counts unit squares (sq cm / sq m)

text.en: Lay square tiles in rows inside a 5 cm by 3 cm rectangle: 3 rows of 5 squares = 5 × 3 = 15 sq cm!
For a square of side s, length and breadth both equal s, so Square Area = side × side.
Watch a classic surprise! Two different rectangles—say 1×11 and 5×7—both have Perimeter 24, yet their Areas are 11 vs 35!

board.text: Same perimeter can give different areas!

text.en: And what about a triangle carved diagonally across a rectangle? Cutting a rectangle in half gives Triangle Area = ½ × base × height!

board.text: Triangle = half rectangle = ½ × b × h

text.en: So before solving any word problem, ask: 'Am I putting ribbon/fence around the edge (Perimeter) or painting/tiling inside (Area)?'

problem.en: A rectangular park is 45 m long and 25 m wide. How much wire fences it once, and how much area needs grass?

text.en: Wire goes around the edge -> compute Perimeter.
Grass covers the ground inside -> compute Area.

why.en: Length/fence is in metres (m), while surface area is in square metres (sq m).

prompt.en: If two rooms have the exact same perimeter of 20 metres, must they also have the same floor area?

requiredIdeas.en: No! A 1 m × 9 m corridor has perimeter 20 m and area 9 sq m.
A 5 m × 5 m room also has perimeter 20 m yet area 25 sq m!

points.en: Rectangle: P = 2(l + b), A = l × b.
Square: P = 4 × side, A = side × side.
Regular polygon (n sides): P = n × side.
Area is measured in square units (cm², m²).
